title: Former Engineering Director Alleges American Express Used "Silent Layoffs" to Move Roles to India
summary:
Public contractor filings show 981 H-1B positions were certified to place workers at American Express from November to June, an increase from 889 the prior year. These records were highlighted by a former Director of Engineering, Simmons, who claims the company spent years shifting roles to India through staffing firms by raising performance expectations for US staff until they could be fired "for cause." The claims coincide with the company's announcement that it is recording a $336 million restructuring charge to eliminate approximately 3,500 positions, or 5% of its global workforce, to reduce management layers and prepare for artificial intelligence.

The job cuts come during a record quarter for the credit card issuer, in which revenue rose 9% to $20.1 billion. On the same day it announced the layoffs, American Express raised its 2026 earnings guidance. Chief Executive Officer Steve Squeri said the workforce reduction is intended to curb rising costs and make the company more agile and efficient. The firm had nearly 77,000 employees at the end of 2025.

American Express is cutting thousands of employees as the leading credit card company prepares for artificial intelligence to take over more of its internal processes.

Amex is eliminating 5% of its global workforce and taking a $336 million restructuring charge, CEO Stephen Squeri told analysts Friday on the company’s third-quarter earnings call. The firm had almost 77,000 employees at the end of 2025.

AMEX IS CUTTING 3,500 JOBS IN A RECORD QUARTER.

That's 5% of its global workforce gone, with a $336M restructuring charge to pay for it. Revenue is $20.1B, up 9%, and Amex just raised guidance. You just can’t make this up anymore. 

The CFO says the goal is to 'reduce layers and increase spans of control' so the company can automate with AI. In plain English, the managers go first and AI comes next.

Barclays cut 5,000 yesterday. Amex cut 3,500 today. Visa reports Tuesday.

This isn't a struggling company trimming. This is what record profits look like now.
$V $AXP
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Visa's layoffs took effect this month: about 2,600 jobs, 7% of the company, mostly tech and product. In a quarter with $11.6B in revenue (up 14%) and $5.6B in profit. 

Six VPs. Thirty-seven senior directors. One campus.

This isn't a struggling company trimming. It's a very profitable one deciding which senior roles it no longer wants to pay for, and moving that money into stablecoins and value-added services. Its closest rival ran the same play six months earlier.

Visa was on my Feb 6 watchlist. Oct 27 earnings: listen for how they talk about headcount.

$V

FORMER AMEX DIRECTOR SAYS AMEX HAS BEEN DOING SILENT LAYOFFS FOR YEARS

Simmons was a Director of Engineering at American Express until a year ago. Simmons says a VP said to raise expectations on engineers until they could be fired "for cause." 

Simmons says the backfill head went to India, usually through "a body shop firm."

AmEx just announced a restructuring that cuts about 5% of its global workforce.

The contractor filings are public. From November through June, outside firms got 981 H-1B filings certified to place workers at AmEx. A year earlier it was 889. 762 list one address, AmEx's Phoenix campus.

Simmons offered to testify. Washington should take that offer.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
I was Director of Engineering at AMEX a year ago. They are doing this so that they can rehire in India. The inside story is MUCH WORSE than that though. 

Amex has been doing silent layoffs for years. As director, the VP told me to gradually increase expectations on engineers so that we could fire them “for cause” When you do this as a leader you get a backfill head to hire for. The caveat at AMEX? The backfill head was already decided for you - they were in India, and usually from a body shop firm. 

Ask me anything about how AMEX is screwing over Americans in the replies. 

@HarmeetKDhillon @andrealucasEEOC @USEEOC I am willing to testify/name names/do whatever is necessary to curb this anti American abuse.

A year ago I wrote: 'AI didn't take your job. Offshoring did.' 

This week a former AmEx engineering director alleges roles were shifted to India through staffing firms while the company talks about AI readiness. 

I'd rather not be right about this one. But here we are.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
A year ago yesterday, I wrote: “AI didn’t take your job. Offshoring did.”

A year later, I have even less patience for the corporate explanations.

In 2022, it was overhiring. Then restructuring. Now it’s AI and efficiency. 🙄

Companies are still eliminating positions in the US while building out similar capabilities offshore…

Of course AI is changing the workforce. But it’s also become a remarkably convenient explanation for decisions that were being made long before generative AI entered the conversation.

I’d pay considerably more attention to the workforce data than the corporate narratives.
